## 2026-09-29 — "User got blacklisted/blocked without doing anything wrong": standard vs hard
Context: backend P1 card, no override, one-line spec, no repro details. "Blacklisted/blocked" maps
to at least three backend mechanisms: simplejwt `token_blacklist` with `ROTATE_REFRESH_TOKENS` +
`BLACKLIST_AFTER_ROTATION` (two concurrent refreshes blacklist each other → forced logout), the
`UserRateThrottle` scopes in `backend/throttles.py` (IP-keyed for anonymous callers, so a shared
NAT/IP can lock out an innocent user at login/signup), and friends `BlockedUser` in
`users/friends.py`. `hard` was defensible (cause unknown, might need the `apiFetch` refresh queue
on the frontend too); `standard` fits once the cause is found — a bounded fix in one area.
Decision: `difficulty: standard`, `areas: backend, auth`, `risk: high` (tokens/throttles/blocking
are all on the high-risk list), `needsDesignRound: true` (security rule: account blocking/abuse),
`engineModel: opus` (risk-high override), `planModel: fable`. The design round's first job is
diagnosis: rank the three mechanisms, name the evidence for the chosen one, and add `frontend` to
the plan only if the root cause is the client refresh race.
Consequences: bias-small held — if the design round finds a multi-area cause, the plan escalates
the scope rather than classify pre-paying for it. Similar vague "I got locked out" cards should get
the same diagnosis-first design round.
